questions.question: Calculate the ampacity of the service conductors for a storage warehouse with a 120/240 V, single-phase service and outside dimensions of 16 m x 10 m. The lighting load is 15 kW and the air-conditioning load is 30 kW.
questions.answer: 189.83 A (source) — verify the warehouse basic W/m² allowance
solution_steps: Rule (non-dwelling service, 8-210): demand = basic load (floor area × the occupancy's W/m² from the basic-load table) + actual loads (lighting/heating/AC, etc.), each with its applicable demand factor.
Floor area = 16 × 10 = 160 m². Connected loads given: lighting 15 kW, air-conditioning 30 kW.
Convert single-phase 240 V: 45 000 ÷ 240 = 187.5 A for the lighting + AC alone; the source's 189.83 A (= 45 559 W ÷ 240) adds a small basic-area allowance for the 160 m².

NEEDS REVIEW: confirm (a) the basic W/m² allowance for a storage warehouse in the 2024 basic-load table and (b) whether the given 15 kW lighting replaces or adds to that basic allowance, and the AC demand factor. Source figure 189.83 A shown; the area allowance could not be verified here.

questions.question: Based on code, what is the maximum voltage drop permitted between the supply side of a consumer service and the point of utilization in any installation?
solution_steps: Rule 8-102: overall voltage drop from the supply side of the consumer's service to the point of utilization shall not exceed 5% of nominal.
Companion limit (don't confuse): any single feeder OR branch circuit shall not exceed 3% — the 5% is the cumulative supply-to-utilization figure asked here.
Result: 5%.

questions.question: A single dwelling unit has a total area of 360 m². It contains a 12 kW electric range, a 6 kW electric dryer, and a 3 kW domestic hot water tank. The main service is 120/240 V, single-phase, 3-wire. Calculate the demand in amps for the main service.
solution_steps: Basic (8-200 1)a)(i)): first 90 m² = 5000 W; remaining 360 − 90 = 270 m² = exactly 3 increments × 1000 W = 3000 W. Basic = 5000 + 3000 = 8000 W.
Range (8-200 1)a)(iv)): 6000 W for first 12 kW + 40% of amount over 12 kW. Range = 12 kW → 6000 W.
Other loads >1500 W with a range present (8-200 1)a)(vii)): 25% of (dryer 6000 + water heater 3000) = 25% × 9000 = 2250 W.
Result: 67.70 A (source figure confirmed by the 2024 method).

questions.question: What size of continuous load can a 1500 A fusible switch supply if the conductors to the load are run in a raceway and the switch is marked for continuous operation at 80% of the rating of its overcurrent devices?
solution_steps: Rule 8-104: a switch not marked for 100% continuous operation may carry a continuous load up to 80% of its overcurrent-device rating.
Result: 1200 A.

questions.question: Determine the minimum ampacity required for the panel feeder conductors of a parking lot that has 200 parking spaces, each with a 15 A duplex receptacle, where the loading is not controlled. The receptacles are supplied from a 120/208 V, 3-phase, 4-wire panel board.
questions.answer: 494.4 A (source) — verify per-space allowance for uncontrolled loading
solution_steps: Rule: parking/automobile-heater receptacle feeders are calculated under Rule 8-400. UNCONTROLLED loading gets little/no demand reduction (vs the reduced figure for controlled loading).
Method: total demand = 200 spaces × the per-space uncontrolled allowance; source uses ≈ 178 080 W (≈ 890 W/space).
Convert 120/208 V 3-phase (√3 because it is a wye 3-phase service): I = 178 080 ÷ (√3 × 208) = 178 080 ÷ 360.3 ≈ 494.4 A.

NEEDS REVIEW: confirm the uncontrolled per-space watt allowance and demand factor under Rule 8-400 in the 2024 code (the √3 conversion is correct; the per-space value drives the answer and was not verified here).

questions.question: Calculate the demand in amps of a single dwelling unit with 190 m² of total area. It contains a 16 kW electric range, a 5 kW electric dryer, a 4 kW domestic hot water tank, and 15 kW of electric baseboard heating. The main service is 120/240 V, single-phase, 3-wire.
solution_steps: Basic (8-200 1)a)(i)): first 90 m² = 5000 W; remaining 190 − 90 = 100 m² → 100/90 = 1.11, round UP to 2 increments × 1000 W = 2000 W. Basic = 7000 W.
Electric heating (8-200 1)a)(v) → Section 62/62-118): 100% of first 10 kW + 75% of remainder = 10 000 + 0.75 × 5000 = 13 750 W. (Not 15 000 W at 100% — the heating demand factor applies.)
Other loads >1500 W with a range present (8-200 1)a)(vii)): 25% of (dryer 5000 + water heater 4000) = 25% × 9000 = 2250 W.
Result: 127.5 A (source figure confirmed; the original step text wrongly stated heating was added at 15 000 W — the 127.5 A answer already reflects the 13 750 W demand figure).

questions.question: A 20 kW electric range is installed in the penthouse suite of a high-rise apartment. What is the demand of the branch circuit?
solution_steps: Rule 8-300 1)a) (BRANCH-circuit range demand, dwelling): a single range counts as 8 kW where its rating ≤ 12 kW, plus 40% of the amount the rating exceeds 12 kW. NOTE: the branch-circuit base is 8 kW — different from the 6 kW base used in the 8-200 SERVICE calc.
Result: 11 200 W (source figure confirmed; the earlier '9200 W via 6 kW base' was the wrong base — 8-300 uses 8 kW).

questions.question: A single-family dwelling is supplied with 120/240 V, single-phase service. It has 250 m² of total area, a 16 kW range, a 4 kW dryer, a 4 kW hot water tank, and 24 kW of electric baseboard heating. Determine the ampacity of the service copper conductors required. Use R90 XLPE 600 V Cu conductors.
solution_steps: Basic (8-200 1)a)(i)): first 90 m² = 5000 W; remaining 250 − 90 = 160 m² → 160/90 = 1.78, round UP to 2 increments × 1000 W = 2000 W. Basic = 7000 W.
Electric heating (Section 62/62-118): 100% of first 10 kW + 75% of remaining 14 kW = 10 000 + 10 500 = 20 500 W.
Other loads >1500 W with a range present (8-200 1)a)(vii)): 25% of (dryer 4000 + water heater 4000) = 25% × 8000 = 2000 W.
Conductor (Table 2, R90 Cu, 75°C terminations per Rule 4-006): 1/0 = 150 A is too small; 2/0 (175 A at 75°C) carries the 154.6 A demand. Result: ≈154.6 A → 2/0 AWG copper.

questions.question: Based on the Canadian Electrical Code, what is the minimum watts per metre demand load for a show-window lighting installation?
solution_steps: Rule 8-200 1)b): show-window lighting demand = 650 W per metre measured along the base of the window.
Result: 650 W/m.

questions.question: What is the minimum demand in watts for the branch circuit conductors supplying a 16 kW range installed in a bakery?
questions.answer: 16 kW (16 000 W) — 100%, no demand reduction for a commercial/non-dwelling range
solution_steps: Rule: the 8-300 range demand REDUCTION applies only to dwelling units. For a range in a commercial/industrial/institutional occupancy (a bakery), the demand is taken at 100% of nameplate (not less than its rating).
Math: demand = 16 kW = 16 000 W.
Result: 16 kW (100%).

questions.question: How much demand load would you provide for a show window in a department store that has a total length of 5 m measured along the base of each window?
solution_steps: Rule 8-200 1)b): show-window lighting = 650 W per metre along the base of the window.
Result: 3250 W.

questions.question: How would you calculate the demand from two loads, 83 kW and 105 kW, which are installed such that only one load at any given time will be connected to the source?
questions.answer: 105 kW — use only the larger of the two non-coincident loads.
solution_steps: Rule 8-106 3): for two loads that cannot operate simultaneously (non-coincident), only the LARGER need be included in the calculation.
Larger of 83 kW and 105 kW = 105 kW.
Result: 105 kW.

questions.question: Determine the demand for the branch circuit conductors supplying a 16 kW range installed in a dwelling unit.
solution_steps: Rule 8-300 1)a) (BRANCH-circuit range demand, dwelling): a single range counts as 8 kW where rating ≤ 12 kW, plus 40% of the amount over 12 kW. (Branch-circuit base = 8 kW, not the 6 kW used in the 8-200 service calc.)
Result: 9600 W (source figure confirmed via the correct 8 kW branch-circuit base).

questions.question: Teck90 cable is installed to supply a 1200 A continuous load. A circuit breaker rated at 80% operation provides overcurrent protection for the circuit. Determine the size of circuit breaker.
solution_steps: Rule 8-104: a breaker not rated for 100% continuous operation must be sized so the continuous load is ≤ 80% of its rating.
Math: required rating = 1200 A ÷ 0.80 = 1500 A.
Result: 1500 A.

questions.question: What is the demand factor for branch circuit conductors supplying electric ranges in the cafeteria of an industrial plant?
questions.answer: 100% — the sum of the ratings of all the electric ranges (no reduction in a non-dwelling occupancy).
solution_steps: Range demand reductions apply to dwelling units; in an industrial cafeteria the ranges are taken at 100% of their combined ratings.
Demand = sum of all range ratings at 100%.
Result: 100%.

questions.question: What are the watts per square metre for the basic load when calculating demand for a theatre?
questions.answer: 30 W/m² (source) — verify against the 2024 basic-load table
solution_steps: Rule (non-dwelling basic load): the basic lighting/area allowance (W/m²) comes from the basic-load table referenced by Rule 8-210.
Value: source gives 30 W/m² for a theatre occupancy.
NEEDS REVIEW: confirm the theatre-occupancy basic W/m² in the 2024 basic-load table (table value not verified here; many occupancies are 30 W/m² but theatre should be checked).

questions.question: A parking garage contains 100 parking spaces, each with a 15 A duplex receptacle, where the loading is controlled. The garage is supplied from a 120/208 V, 3-phase, 4-wire feeder. What is the minimum ampacity required for the feeder conductors?
questions.answer: 54 000 W → 149.89 A (source) — verify per-space allowance for controlled loading
solution_steps: Rule: parking/automobile-heater receptacle feeders → Rule 8-400. CONTROLLED loading permits a reduced demand per space.
Method: source gives total controlled demand = 54 000 W for 100 spaces (= 540 W/space).

NEEDS REVIEW: confirm the controlled per-space watt allowance / demand factor under Rule 8-400 in the 2024 code (the √3 conversion and 54 000 ÷ 360.3 math are correct; per-space value not verified here).

questions.question: A building 20 m x 100 m has one half used as a beauty salon and the other half as a bank. What is the minimum service demand for this building?
questions.answer: Sum of each occupancy's area load at its own basic W/m² (each half = 1000 m²), then add.
solution_steps: Rule (non-dwelling, 8-210): basic demand = floor area × the occupancy's basic W/m² (from the Table-14 basic-load list); compute each occupancy separately because the W/m² differs.
Area: 20 × 100 = 2000 m² total → beauty salon = 1000 m², bank = 1000 m².
Method: demand = (1000 m² × salon W/m²) + (1000 m² × bank W/m²) + any specific equipment loads, each at its demand factor.
NEEDS REVIEW: needs the 2024 basic W/m² for 'beauty salon' and 'bank/office' from the basic-load table to produce a single number (table values not verified here).

questions.question: A two-story building 100 m x 20 m has a restaurant on the lower floor and a beauty salon on the second floor. The restaurant has a 28 kW power load and the beauty salon a 22 kW power load. What is the total service demand for this building?
questions.answer: Sum of each floor's basic area load plus the 28 kW and 22 kW power loads (per occupancy, then add).
solution_steps: Rule (non-dwelling, 8-210): demand per occupancy = floor area × its basic W/m² (Table-14 basic-load list) + the connected power loads at their demand factors.
Area: each floor = 100 × 20 = 2000 m².
Method: total = (2000 m² × restaurant W/m² + 28 kW) + (2000 m² × salon W/m² + 22 kW).
NEEDS REVIEW: needs the 2024 basic W/m² for 'restaurant' and 'beauty salon' to produce a single number (table values not verified here).

questions.question: An industrial complex has a covered area of 3000 m². There is 500 kW of power loads plus a 500 kW electric space-heating load. The service is 600/347 V, 3-phase, 4-wire. Determine the calculated service demand in amps.
questions.answer: I = total demand W ÷ (√3 × 600 V) — combine area load + 500 kW power + heating demand, then convert.
solution_steps: Rule (non-dwelling, 8-210): basic area load = 3000 m² × the occupancy's basic W/m² (Table-14 basic-load list).
Add: 500 kW power load (at 100% / its demand factor) + 500 kW electric space heating (Section 62/62-118: 100% of first 10 kW + 75% of remainder for the heating portion, as applicable).
Convert: 600/347 V is a wye 3-phase service → I = total demand W ÷ (√3 × 600).

NEEDS REVIEW: needs the 2024 basic W/m² for the occupancy and confirmation of the industrial heating demand treatment to give a single number (the √3 × 600 conversion is correct; table value not verified here).

questions.question: What is the maximum amount of load when a 120 V baseboard heater is connected to a 15 A circuit breaker rated for 80% operation?
solution_steps: Rule 8-104: continuous load limit = 80% of breaker rating → 15 A × 0.80 = 12 A.
Result: 1440 W (12 A continuous).

questions.question: Determine the minimum conductor ampacity required for a 240 V, 14.4 kW range installed in a commercial kitchen.
solution_steps: Rule: a range in a commercial kitchen (non-dwelling) is taken at 100% of nameplate, no demand reduction.
Conductor ampacity must be at least 60 A.
Result: 60 A.

questions.question: When feeding a 240 V, 30 A load at a distance of 60 m, which size copper conductor is required to limit voltage drop to 2%?
questions.answer: #4 AWG by calculation (source said #6 AWG — see note)
solution_steps: Allowed drop = 2% × 240 V = 4.8 V.
Vd = 2 × k × L × I ÷ cmil, with k ≈ 12.9 Ω·cmil/ft (copper), one-way L = 60 m = 196.85 ft, I = 30 A.
Conclusion: the smallest copper conductor meeting the 2% limit is #4 AWG (option B), NOT #6. Source answer #6 (option C) gives 5.81 V and violates the 2% limit.
NEEDS REVIEW: confirm against the exact Table D3 mV/A·m coefficients in the 2024 code; both the source figure (#6) and the calculated figure (#4) are shown so a human can decide.

questions.question: What minimum size consumer's service is required for a 120/240 V single-phase dwelling that has a floor area of 85 m²?
solution_steps: Rule 8-200 1)b): a single dwelling with floor area (excl. basement) of 80 m² or more requires a minimum service of 24 000 W / 100 A; less than 80 m² → minimum 14 400 W / 60 A.
Area = 85 m² (≥ 80 m²) → minimum 100 A.
Result: 24,000 W / 100 A (option B).

questions.question: A 24 V DC branch circuit of remote lamps using #8 copper conductors has a connected load of 144 watts. What is the maximum distance permitted for a 5% voltage drop? (Hint: multiply 0.86 by k for extra-low voltage.)
solution_steps: I = 144 W ÷ 24 V = 6 A; allowed drop = 5% × 24 V = 1.2 V.
Vd = (2 × k × L × I) ÷ cmil; ELV adjustment multiplies k by 0.86 (k ≈ 0.86 × 12.9 ≈ 11.1). #8 = 16 510 cmil.
Result: ≈ 45.78 m (option D) — matches the calculation.

questions.question: 600 V is measured at the supply side of the consumer's service. What is the minimum allowable voltage at a HVAC unit rated for 600 V operation?
solution_steps: Rule 8-102: maximum overall voltage drop supply-to-utilization = 5% of nominal.
Math: 5% × 600 V = 30 V drop → minimum voltage at the unit = 600 − 30 = 570 V.
Result: 570 V (option B).

questions.question: Maximum distance from an emergency lamp given: 12 V, 100 W, cable #10 AWG, and maximum voltage drop 2%? (Hint: multiply 0.86 by k for extra-low voltage.)
solution_steps: I = 100 W ÷ 12 V = 8.33 A; allowed drop = 2% × 12 V = 0.24 V.
Vd = (2 × k × L × I) ÷ cmil; ELV adjustment multiplies k by 0.86 (k ≈ 11.1). #10 ≈ 10 380 cmil.
Result: ≈ 4.15 m (option B) — matches the calculation.
